title: Autonomous Multi-Agent DevOps & SRE Incident Remediation Engine
tagline: Self-healing production infra powered by collaborative LLM agents with sandboxed code validation.
whyItStandsOut: Recruiters and hiring managers in 2025/2026 look beyond basic chatbot wrappers. Building an autonomous multi-agent system that executes deterministic bash/code actions inside isolated Docker containers with automated rollback demonstrates distributed systems, security, and bleeding-edge agent orchestration (LangGraph/AutoGen).

architecture.overview: A distributed supervisor-worker multi-agent architecture. When an alert fires (via webhook), the Supervisor agent delegates diagnosis, environment reproduction, patch generation, and regression verification across specialized agents.
components: Telemetry Ingest: Receives alerts from Prometheus/Datadog or OpenTelemetry traces via FastAPI webhook.
Supervisor Agent: Maintains incident state graph; routes sub-tasks to Triager, Coder, and Verifier agents.
Triager Agent: Analyzes stack traces, correlates distributed logs, and performs git bisect to isolate faulty commit.
Sandbox Executor: Spins up ephemeral isolated Docker container with the target repo revision.
Coder Agent: Synthesizes minimal fix with unit test cases using AST context.
Verifier Agent: Executes test suite in sandbox container; verifies fix resolves incident without regressions.
PR & Rollback Manager: Automatically creates GitHub PR with incident post-mortem analysis and patch diff.

milestones.task: Set up FastAPI webhook and Docker SDK sandbox manager to spawn disposable container testbeds with resource limits (cgroups).
Implement LangGraph state graph with Supervisor, Log Analyzer, and Code Patching agents.
Integrate Git bisect automation and Tree-sitter AST extraction to feed relevant code slices to the LLM context window.
Build automated test execution runner inside container with structured error capture and multi-turn iterative self-correction.
Add GitHub PR automation with structured markdown incident post-mortems and benchmark against 20 real GitHub bug issues.

resumeBullets: Architected an autonomous multi-agent incident remediation engine utilizing LangGraph and Docker SDK, reducing mean-time-to-resolution (MTTR) by 42% across simulated microservice outages.
Engineered an ephemeral sandbox execution runtime with cgroups isolation to validate generated security patches and automated test suites with 0% host risk.
Implemented an AST-guided prompt compression pipeline using Tree-sitter, reducing LLM token consumption by 65% while maintaining 91% patch compilation rate.
Designed automated Git bisect and log correlation agents that pinpointed breaking commit hashes within 45 seconds of alert ingestion.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you prevent the autonomous agent from hallucinating destructive bash commands or deleting databases?
interviewQuestions.a: We enforce strict defense-in-depth: all agent execution is confined to non-root, read-only rootfs Docker containers with drop-capabilities (cap-drop=ALL), isolated network bridges, and a deterministic command allowlist verified by an execution proxy before invocation.

interviewQuestions.q: How did you manage agent cyclic loops or deadlocks in LangGraph?
interviewQuestions.a: We implemented a strict state machine with MaxIterations guardrails, exponential backoff on retry, and a human-in-the-loop fallback hook when the Verifier agent detects the test suite failing 3 consecutive iterations.

title: Enterprise Multimodal GraphRAG Knowledge & Citation Platform
tagline: Hybrid Knowledge Graph + Vector Retrieval engine with sub-300ms latency and zero hallucinated citations.
whyItStandsOut: Standard naive RAG (chunking + cosine similarity) has become a dime-a-dozen project. Engineering a hybrid GraphRAG system that extracts entities/relations into a Neo4j graph, links them with dense embeddings, and performs cross-encoder re-ranking demonstrates deep understanding of production-grade NLP, data structures, and graph theory.

architecture.overview: A dual-path retrieval architecture combining structured Knowledge Graph traversals (Cypher queries) with unstructured dense/sparse vector search (hybrid BM25 + Qdrant), fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and reranked via cross-encoders.
components: Document Parsing Pipeline: Parses PDFs, markdown, and tables with layout-aware chunking (Docling / Unstructured).
Entity & Relation Extractor: Uses LLM with structured JSON output schema to extract (Subject, Predicate, Object) triplets.
Graph Storage (Neo4j): Stores knowledge nodes, relationships, and property graphs.
Vector Index (Qdrant): Indexes text chunks with BGE-large dense vectors and BM25 sparse vectors.
Hybrid Retrieval Orchestrator: Executes multi-hop graph neighborhood expansion combined with vector search.
RRF & Cross-Encoder Reranker: Blends and scores retrieved candidates using BGE-Reranker-Large.
Hallucination Verification: Verifies every generated claim directly against extracted document citation spans.

milestones.task: Set up Neo4j and Qdrant in Docker; build document ingestion pipeline with layout-aware PDF chunking.
Implement asynchronous triplet extraction pipeline with schema validation and entity deduplication.
Develop hybrid retrieval engine fusing Cypher graph traversals with vector similarity using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
Integrate BGE cross-encoder re-ranking and citation span attribution check for factual grounding.
Build React dashboard with interactive Neo4j graph visualization (using react-force-graph) and evaluate on RAGTriad metrics using TruLens.

resumeBullets: Built an enterprise GraphRAG platform combining Neo4j knowledge graphs and Qdrant vector search, achieving a 38% increase in multi-hop question-answering accuracy over baseline vector RAG.
Designed an asynchronous entity-relation extraction pipeline handling 25,000+ pages with parallel batching and Pydantic schema validation.
Implemented Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and cross-encoder re-ranking (BGE-Reranker-Large), cutting context noise by 52% and reducing response latency to 320ms.
Established automated RAG evaluation using TruLens (faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision), achieving a 96.4% groundedness score across 500 enterprise domain queries.

interviewQuestions.q: Why combine Knowledge Graphs with Vector Search instead of using Vector Search alone?
interviewQuestions.a: Vector search excels at semantic fuzzy matching on short queries, but fails at multi-hop reasoning (e.g. 'Which suppliers of Company X were affected by the 2024 logistics regulation?'). Knowledge graphs model explicit discrete relationships and hierarchical structures, allowing deterministic graph hops that vectors miss.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you solve entity deduplication when different documents refer to the same entity with slight variations?
interviewQuestions.a: We run an entity resolution pass using embedding cosine similarity above 0.92 coupled with Levenshtein string distance and an LLM verification step for ambiguous matches, merging nodes into a canonical entity with alias properties in Neo4j.

title: Ultra-Low Latency Full-Duplex Multimodal AI Copilot
tagline: Real-time voice and vision assistant with WebRTC, bidirectional audio streaming, and sub-250ms end-to-end latency.
whyItStandsOut: Voice AI in 2025/2026 demands instantaneous full-duplex conversations with natural interruptions, not awkward push-to-talk delays. Building a WebRTC-based streaming pipeline with VAD (Voice Activity Detection), streaming STT, LLM token streaming, and streaming TTS demonstrates distributed networking, audio buffer management, and concurrency.

architecture.overview: Full-duplex real-time media streaming using WebRTC. Audio tracks and video frames flow asynchronously through a pipelined audio processing loop that supports instant human barge-in interruption.
components: WebRTC Ingestion (LiveKit): Low-latency UDP-based peer-to-peer audio and video transport.
Silero Voice Activity Detector (VAD): Detects human speech onset and termination in <20ms.
Streaming STT (Deepgram/Whisper streaming): Converts audio chunks to interim and final text transcripts over WebSockets.
Vision Context Processor: Periodically extracts keyframes using OpenCV and sends compressed visual embeddings.
Async LLM Streamer: Generates response tokens with streaming yield; immediately cancelled upon barge-in signal.
Streaming TTS Engine: Synthesizes audio buffer frames incrementally from initial tokens with First-Audio-Packet latency under 120ms.

milestones.task: Set up LiveKit server and React WebRTC audio/video capture client.
Implement Silero VAD audio frame buffer and WebSocket streaming to Deepgram STT.
Integrate asynchronous LLM token generation with sentence-boundary chunking for TTS streaming.
Implement bidirectional barge-in interruption logic (flushing audio output buffer when user speaks).
Add camera frame contextual QA and benchmark end-to-end voice-to-voice latency.

resumeBullets: Architected a full-duplex multimodal conversational assistant utilizing WebRTC and LiveKit, achieving sub-240ms voice-to-voice end-to-end latency.
Implemented an asynchronous sentence-boundary streaming pipeline integrating Deepgram STT, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Cartesia TTS with zero blocking I/O.
Designed a robust interruption handling mechanism using Silero VAD that flushes outbound audio buffers within 35ms of user barge-in.
Integrated real-time video keyframe downsampling with OpenCV to provide live computer vision question answering over webcam feeds at 1 FPS.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you achieve sub-300ms end-to-end latency in a voice loop?
interviewQuestions.a: By aggressive pipelining and eliminating batch boundaries: 1) Stream raw PCM audio directly via WebRTC. 2) Stream STT transcripts incrementally. 3) Feed the first clause/sentence (punctuation-aware chunker) into streaming TTS before the LLM finishes generating the entire response. 4) Use edge-hosted low-latency providers (Cartesia Sonic, Deepgram Nova-2).

interviewQuestions.q: What happens when a user interrupts the bot while it is speaking?
interviewQuestions.a: Silero VAD detects incoming speech above energy and probability thresholds, triggering an immediate cancellation token on the LLM async generator and issuing a WebRTC track silence flush command to purge already-buffered audio chunks.

title: Autonomous AI Code Reviewer & Semantic Vulnerability Patcher
tagline: Static analysis + LLM-driven SAST engine that detects OWASP vulnerabilities, synthesizes verified patches, and generates unit tests.
whyItStandsOut: Developer productivity tools and automated code security are among the highest-funded and most sought-after domains in tech. Combining AST analysis (Tree-sitter) with Semgrep rules and LLM synthesis shows expertise in compilers, software security, and evaluation benchmarks.

architecture.overview: GitHub App event trigger -> PR diff analysis -> Semgrep AST rule scan -> Vulnerability contextualization -> LLM patch synthesis -> Docker sandbox test verification -> Inline GitHub review comment.
components: GitHub App Listener: Webhook captures `pull_request.opened` and `pull_request.synchronize` events.
Diff & AST Parser: Extracts changed functions, imports, and symbol call graphs using Tree-sitter.
Rule Engine (Semgrep): Scans for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XSS, SSRF, IDOR).
Context Builder: Injects function definition, callers, and surrounding unit tests into LLM prompt.
Patch & Test Synthesizer: Generates minimal secure diff and regression test reproducing the exploit.
Sandbox Runner: Verifies tests pass and vulnerability is closed in a containerized runner.
Inline PR Reporter: Posts formatted GitHub review comments with 1-click 'Apply Suggestion' button.

milestones.task: Configure GitHub App with webhook receiver and parse unified PR diffs.
Integrate Semgrep engine and Tree-sitter for syntax tree navigation and taint tracking.
Build LLM prompt orchestration for contextual security patch synthesis and regression test generation.
Implement Docker test runner to automatically verify generated test passes with patch applied.
Deploy GitHub App on cloud VM and benchmark against OWASP benchmark test suite.

resumeBullets: Built a production GitHub App that automatically detects code vulnerabilities and synthesizes verified patches across 4 programming languages.
Integrated Semgrep static taint analysis with Tree-sitter AST parsing, eliminating 70% of irrelevant code lines before LLM prompt injection.
Automated patch verification via containerized test execution, achieving an 84% first-time compile and test pass rate on 200 synthetic security flaws.
Deployed to 15+ open-source repositories, analyzing over 1,200 pull requests with an average analysis latency of under 18 seconds.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you prevent false positives from flooding developer pull requests?
interviewQuestions.a: We use a hybrid funnel: Semgrep flags potential taint paths, but before creating a comment, the LLM runs a verification pass against the surrounding call hierarchy. If the input is already sanitized by an upstream middleware or type constraint, the finding is silently discarded.

interviewQuestions.q: How does Tree-sitter improve the code review pipeline compared to sending raw diffs?
interviewQuestions.a: Raw diffs lack semantic scope (a 2-line change inside a 500-line method). Tree-sitter parses the full syntax tree to extract the enclosing function, class definition, docstrings, and imported types, giving the LLM complete semantic context without exceeding token budgets.

title: Offline-First Edge LLM Studio with WebGPU & Speculative Decoding
tagline: Private, zero-server AI workspace running quantized 7B LLMs in the browser at 30+ tokens/sec using WebGPU.
whyItStandsOut: Edge AI and local on-device inference are key frontiers as organizations seek to reduce cloud GPU costs and guarantee absolute data privacy. Demonstrating browser-native WebGPU, quantized weights (AWQ/GGUF/Wasm), and client-side vector search (Vectorlite/OPFS) showcases systems programming and web graphics performance.

architecture.overview: Runs quantized models (e.g. Llama-3-8B-Instruct-q4f16, Mistral-7B, Phi-3.5) directly inside the client's GPU via WebGPU, caching model weights in the browser's OPFS with zero server compute costs.
components: WebGPU Inference Engine (WebLLM / Wasm): Compiles tensor operations to compute shaders executing on client GPU.
Storage Manager (OPFS): Streams and caches multi-gigabyte quantized GGUF/safetensors weights in local browser cache.
Client-Side Vector DB: Executes local embedding generation and vector similarity search inside a Web Worker.
Speculative Decoding Pipeline: Uses a tiny 0.5B draft model to speculate tokens, verified in parallel by the target 7B model.
Streaming Token Dispatcher: Renders tokens at 60 FPS using RequestAnimationFrame and smooth text interpolation.

milestones.task: Set up WebGPU device context detection and WebLLM pipeline with Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct-q4.
Implement Origin Private File System (OPFS) storage manager with progressive model chunk downloading and progress bar.
Build client-side in-browser RAG using Transformers.js for local embeddings and in-memory cosine index.
Implement speculative decoding / prompt caching to accelerate output token generation speed.
Measure and optimize memory footprint, ensuring sub-2.5GB VRAM usage on laptop GPUs.

resumeBullets: Engineered a privacy-first edge AI web application executing 8B parameter LLMs entirely client-side via WebGPU with 0 bytes transmitted to cloud servers.
Implemented an Origin Private File System (OPFS) streaming cache manager, enabling instantaneous model boot-up from browser disk cache on repeat visits.
Achieved 34 tokens/sec inference speed on Apple M-series and RTX laptop GPUs by optimizing 4-bit weight quantization and compute shaders.
Integrated client-side Web Worker embedding generation and vector search over user-uploaded PDF documents with zero latency penalty on the UI thread.

interviewQuestions.q: What are the primary technical constraints of running LLMs in the browser via WebGPU?
interviewQuestions.a: 1) VRAM limits: Browsers have max buffer size and allocation limits (often 2-4GB per process), requiring aggressive 4-bit (AWQ/q4f16) quantization. 2) Memory bandwidth: Browser memory copies between CPU and GPU need to be minimized using unified memory architectures or shared array buffers. 3) Initial download size: Requiring progressive chunked downloads and persistent OPFS caching.

interviewQuestions.q: How does Speculative Decoding work to increase inference throughput?
interviewQuestions.a: Autoregressive generation is memory-bandwidth bound. Speculative decoding runs a tiny fast draft model (e.g. 0.5B) to generate K draft tokens in rapid succession, then passes all K tokens through the large target model (e.g. 8B) in a single parallel forward pass. The target model verifies and accepts or rejects the tokens, achieving 2-3x speedups without changing the output probability distribution.
